sources: FRIDAY NOV 6 2026 PRE-OPEN RUN at 07:15 UTC, which is 02:15 ET, so US cash markets are SHUT, the jobs report is six hours away and the only live prices are oil, metals and the dollar from the Asian session. FIRST THING TO READ: THE DASHBOARD HAD BEEN FROZEN SINCE NOV 2. Git HEAD was still 3e5ece7, the Nov 2 commit, and data.json was last written Nov 2 07:19 - THREE SCHEDULED RUNS (NOV 3, NOV 4, NOV 5) PRODUCED NO COMMIT. Cause found and fixed: .git/HEAD.lock and .git/objects/maintenance.lock, both stamped Nov 2 07:19, had been blocking every ref update since, and the script auto-cleaner could not delete them because the session lacked delete permission. Permission was requested and granted this run, both locks removed, commit and push completed. The lock-file problem flagged on and off for the last several weeks is therefore REAL and RECURRING, not self-healing as the Nov 2 run concluded. HEADLINE: THE AI COMPLEX BROKE PROPERLY ON NOV 5 AND THE WAR PREMIUM IN OIL IS GONE. Equity vol is at its highest close since March, credit is wider than a week ago, copper-gold has collapsed, and the real economy data printed STRONGER. VOL - THE BIG MOVE. VIX CLOSED 28.18 ON NOV 5, UP ABOUT 70 PCT, its highest close since MARCH 30, intraday high 28.09 cited by CNBC. Against 19.42 a week ago the tile is UP and this is a genuine regime change, not the round trip the last three runs described. The session: NASDAQ COMPOSITE MINUS 5.5 PCT INTO CORRECTION TERRITORY, S&P 500 minus 4.4 pct, DOW MINUS 3.4 PCT or about 1,833 POINTS, wiping out the post-election gains of the previous day. Trigger was political, not macro: Democratic wins in the Nov 3 midterms read as a slower path for AI development. Nvidia minus 9 pct, AMD MINUS 17 PCT, the iShares Semiconductor ETF minus 12 pct, QUALCOMM MINUS 19 PCT on a weak outlook tied to a memory-component shortage, Tesla and SpaceX down on scrutiny concerns. Ten-year yield 4.84 pct, down from 4.89 pct at the Wednesday close. A strategist quoted by Yahoo cautioned that vol has NOT yet reached capitulation or contrarian extremes. OIL - THE RISK PREMIUM UNWOUND, AND IT IS THE LARGEST WEEKLY FALL ON THE BOARD. Brent about 100.30 USD, PLUS 2 PCT on the day, WTI 91.80 USD plus 1.5 pct, both bouncing off the lows after fresh TANKER ATTACKS, but BOTH BENCHMARKS ARE HEADING FOR A WEEKLY DECLINE OF ABOUT 12 PCT. Against the 110.00 tile on Nov 2 the arrow is DOWN and this is the completion of the move the last run flagged as starting: for fourteen runs the oil tile only rose on escalation, then it gave back the entire Gulf premium in four sessions. Note the conflict in sources: tokenpost quotes Brent at 98.82 plus 1 pct for the same session, so read the tile as 99-100, not as a precise 100.30. HORMUZ RISK HAS NOT GONE AWAY - fxempire is running a Hormuz-risk forecast and tanker attacks are what lifted prices back over 100. CREDIT - THE QUESTION FROM THREE RUNS AGO IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER WAS THE BAD ONE. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 finally posted the Oct 30 print at 3.44 PCT, i.e. 344bp - WIDER than the 326bp carried, not near it. So OCT 30 WAS CREDIT CONTAGION, NOT AN ISOLATED AI-EQUITY RESET, exactly the test the last three runs said was the cleanest on the board. The series then came back in: 3.43 Nov 2, 3.40 Nov 3, 3.32 Nov 4, page updated Nov 5 09:08 CST. Tile 332bp. Against 326bp a week ago the arrow is UP. CRITICAL GAP: THE NOV 5 PRINT - THE DAY OF THE 4.4 PCT S&P DROP AND THE 70 PCT VIX SPIKE - IS NOT YET POSTED and is the single most important number due today. If it breaks above 344bp this is a credit event; if it holds near 332bp the equity move is still contained. CURVE - FLATTENING OFF THE HIGH, FIRST DOWN ARROW IN FIVE RUNS. FRED T10Y2Y Nov 4 at 0.32 (0.34 Nov 3, 0.32 Nov 2, 0.38 Oct 30, 0.37 Oct 29), updated Nov 4 16:03 CST, series metadata confirms Nov 4 is the last observation so the Nov 5 print is pending. Against 0.38 a week ago that is MINUS 6bp and the tile turns DOWN after four consecutive UP runs. Still comfortably positive and nowhere near inversion. BREAKEVEN - FLAT, AND THIS IS THE SURPRISE. FRED T5YIFR Nov 5 at 2.22 pct (2.22 Nov 4, 2.21 Nov 3, 2.19 Nov 2, 2.22 Oct 30), updated Nov 5 16:03 CST. Against 2.22 a week ago, FLAT. The last run predicted this arrow would turn DOWN if oil held near 110 - OIL FELL 12 PCT AND THE BREAKEVEN DID NOT BUDGE. Either the market does not believe the oil move sticks, or underlying inflation expectations are firmer than the crude price suggests. Worth watching against the 75.2 ISM prices index. METALS - COPPER-GOLD COLLAPSES TO 1.53 AND THE COMPOSITION IS NOW CLEAN RISK-OFF. Spot gold 4,063.39 USD, minus 0.6 pct on the Nov 6 session but UP ABOUT 4 PCT ON THE WEEK from 3,900, having bounced hard off the one-year low. Copper 6.2114 USD/lb, minus 0.6 pct on the day, MINUS 5.8 PCT ON THE MONTH and minus about 6.2 pct over four weeks. The ratio reads 1.5287, so the tile goes 1.66 to 1.53 and the arrow turns DOWN after five UP runs. THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE WARNING CARRIED FOR THE LAST FIVE RUNS: the ratio was high because gold was collapsing, and now it is low because gold is bid and copper is being sold. Gold up, copper down, equity vol at 28 - that is a coherent flight to safety and the cleanest risk-off signal on the board. DOLLAR - FLAT FOR A FIFTH RUN AND NOW GENUINELY STRANGE. DXY 101.691, plus 0.09 pct on the Nov 6 session. Against 102.05 a week ago that is MINUS 0.36, which still reads FLAT. The S&P fell 4.4 pct in a single session, the Nasdaq entered a correction, gold rallied 4 pct on the week - AND THE DOLLAR DID NOT CATCH A BID. Five runs of this now. Either the December hike pricing is wrong or the dollar is, and a risk-off session that does not move the dollar is the strongest version of that contradiction so far. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - TIGHTENING AT THE MARGIN FOR A THIRD WEEK, STILL LOOSE. NFCI minus 0.459 for the week ending OCT 30 (minus 0.467 Oct 23, minus 0.477 Oct 16, minus 0.487 Oct 9, minus 0.498 Oct 2), updated Nov 4 07:37 CST. Tile minus 0.46 and the arrow turns UP, i.e. tightening, for the first time in many runs - three consecutive weekly moves toward zero. This is the FIRST NFCI containing the Oct 30 vol, and it does NOT contain Nov 5. Conditions are still clearly easy by level; the direction has changed. Next update Wednesday Nov 11 and that one will contain the Nov 5 selloff. LABOUR - THE STRONGEST PRINT ON THE BOARD, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE PRICE ACTION. Initial claims 189k for the week ending OCT 31, released Nov 5 (prior week revised UP to 195k, four-week average down to 194.75k from 197.00k), reported as near 57-YEAR LOWS with layoffs subdued; continuing claims edged higher. Against 194k a week ago the arrow is DOWN, i.e. improving. Note FRED ICSA HTML still showed 194k for Oct 24 when fetched this run - the 189k figure comes from the DOL release and secondary reporting, not from a refreshed FRED page. NO LABOUR CRACK WHATSOEVER. ISM - ACCELERATING. OCTOBER MANUFACTURING PMI 55.5 PCT, released Nov 2, UP FROM 54.5 in September, with the PRICES INDEX STILL AT 75.2. Tile 55.5, arrow UP. Manufacturing expanded faster in October, which is the second hard data point this run arguing the real economy is fine. MACRO TILES - ALL CARRIED, AND TWO OF THEM LAND TODAY. Consumer sentiment 48.0, UMich OCTOBER FINAL, revised UP from a 46.3 preliminary; the NOVEMBER PRELIMINARY IS DUE TODAY AT 15:00 GMT, 10:00 ET, i.e. AFTER THIS RUN. The real economy printed STRONGER this week - ISM accelerating to 55.5, claims at 189k near a 57-year low, financial conditions still loose at minus 0.46, breakeven steady at 2.22 despite a 12 pct fall in crude, no recession signal anywhere in the macro tiles. This is still a FINANCIAL-MARKET event driven by AI-equity positioning and a political re-pricing, NOT a macro event. The thing that would convert it is credit. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: the NOV 5 HY OAS PRINT and whether it exceeds 344bp; TODAY PAYROLLS against a labour market that still looks pristine; whether VIX 28 holds or fades, given the capitulation caveat; UMich preliminary today after a five-month low; getting a live MOVE print, now the most expensive blind spot; whether December Fed hike pricing survived a 4.4 pct S&P day; whether the dollar ever responds to anything; Hormuz and whether the tanker attacks rebuild an oil premium; and keeping the git locks clear so the dashboard does not silently freeze for another three days.
